name: Evidence gate for chat answers
owner_decision: Bambang 2026-09-25: chat answers go through a hook; an answer that fails is held and must be corrected (not only warned).
single_source: This file is the ONLY place the G-03 rules are written. scripts/hooks/g03.py reads it; SKILL.md files point here.
binds: Every text Claude writes to the owner in the current turn (from the owner's latest message to the end of the turn). Enforced by the Stop hook scripts/hooks/stop.py: the turn cannot end while a check fails.
evidence: A token counts as verified only when it appears in a real tool result of this session (the transcript) or in the owner's own messages. A `code` token may also match the name of a tool that was called successfully, or a path / command such a call was given. Hook messages and Claude's own text are never evidence.

checks.name: TOKENS_FROM_A_SOURCE
checks.rule: Every checkable token in the answer (token_kinds below) appears in some tool result of this session or in an owner message, unless its sentence carries the unverified marker.

checks.name: OUTSIDE_SYSTEMS_READ_LIVE
checks.rule: A sentence that names an outside system (system_rules) and carries a token of the listed kinds: every such token appears in the result of a tool that reads that system directly (not a local copy), unless the sentence carries the unverified marker. 2026-09-25: a GitHub branch was reported as existing at 22bdede from a stale local git ref.

checks.name: ABSENCE_NEEDS_A_SOURCE
checks.rule: A sentence with absence wording (absence_phrases) carries the unverified marker, or holds at least one token that passes T1 (and T2 where it applies).

checks.name: CORRECTION_AFTER_A_HOLD
checks.rule: A text that fails T1-T3 is not unsaid. Each of its problems is resolved only by a later text in the same turn that starts with correction_prefix, itself passes T1-T3, and restates the failing token (T1/T2) or absence phrase (T3), verified or with the unverified marker.

override: Only the owner can type it. When the owner's latest message contains it, the Stop hook lets that turn's answer through unchecked. If g03.py itself fails, the answer is held (fail closed) until it is fixed or the owner overrides.

token_kinds.commit: git commit id: 7-40 hex characters holding both a digit and a letter a-f
token_kinds.workflow_id: 16 characters, letters and digits, mixed case (n8n workflow id)
token_kinds.number: any other number written with digits
token_kinds.code: inline `code` without spaces (a path, branch, file or field name); `file.py:120` must be a Read of that file that showed line 120
token_kinds.quote: text between "...", “...” or 「...」: found verbatim (whitespace and markup ignored) in a source

skip: fenced code blocks (``` ... ```): commands and examples, not claims
sentences that carry the unverified marker
known_limits: A token found in a source proves the token exists there, not that the sentence reads it correctly.
Sentences without a checkable token (plain wording, no id, number, date or code) cannot be checked, except for absence wording (T3).
Small numbers are found in almost any tool result, so T1 is weak for them.
System detection (T2) is a word list per sentence; a sentence about GitHub that never says GitHub / origin/ / remote is not bound by T2.
Hooks run as the same OS user as the model: they stop shortcuts and forgetting, not a deliberate attack.
